title: In 1 Corinthians 6 What Implications Does The Idea Of The Body As A Temple Of The Holy Spirit Have For Our Daily Lives And Choices
paragraphs: Understanding the Body as a Temple of the Holy Spirit: Insights from 1 Corinthians 6
The apostle Paul’s statement in 1 Corinthians 6:19 is one of the most profound teachings concerning the Christian’s physical body:
Or know ye not that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit which is in you, which ye have from God? and ye are not your own; - 1 Corinthians 6:19 ASV
This declaration carries deep theological and practical significance. Let’s explore what this means for our everyday lives, particularly in the context Paul addresses.
The Context: Fleeing Sexual Immorality

Paul wrote to believers in Corinth—a city known for its moral laxity and pagan worship practices. He warns against sexual immorality, emphasizing that how we use our bodies matters to God. In verses prior, he says:
Flee fornication. Every sin that a man doeth is without the body; but he that committeth fornication sinneth against his own body. - 1 Corinthians 6:18 ASV
Paul’s reasoning is not merely moral but theological: the believer’s body is indwelt by the Holy Spirit.
Implications for Daily Life
1. Our Bodies Belong to God

Paul reminds us, "ye are not your own; for ye were bought with a price" (1 Corinthians 6:19-20). Through Christ’s sacrificial death, believers are redeemed, and our lives—including our bodies—are no longer ours to use as we wish. This truth calls us to steward our bodies in a way that honors God.
2. A Call to Holiness and Purity
Understanding that the Holy Spirit dwells within us should motivate us toward holiness. The body, as God’s temple, is set apart for His purposes. Paul urges elsewhere:
I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable to God, which is your spiritual service. - Romans 12:1 ASV
This encompasses sexual purity, but also extends to every area: what we consume, how we care for our health, and the ways we use our bodies to serve others.
3. The Sacredness of Ordinary Life

Since the Holy Spirit dwells in us, every aspect of our daily existence is sacred. Even mundane tasks can be done "as unto the Lord" (Colossians 3:23 ASV). This perspective transforms our approach to work, rest, relationships, and recreation.
4. Communal Implications

While Paul focuses here on the individual body, elsewhere he describes the church as a collective temple (1 Corinthians 3:16). Our personal holiness contributes to the health and witness of the larger body of Christ.
Practical Applications
Guarding What Enters: What we watch, listen to, or consume matters. We are to pursue purity in all things (Philippians 4:8).
Healthy Living: Caring for our bodies honors God as Creator and Redeemer (Psalm 139:14).
Sexual Integrity: Fleeing immorality and honoring marriage reflects God’s design and the Spirit’s presence in us (Hebrews 13:4).
Service: Using our bodies to serve others manifests the love and presence of Christ (Galatians 5:13).
The Ultimate Motivation: Glorifying God
For ye were bought with a price: glorify God therefore in your body. - 1 Corinthians 6:20 ASV
The overarching purpose is to glorify God in all we do with our bodies. This flows from gratitude for Christ’s redemptive work and the indwelling presence of the Holy Spirit.
Conclusion

Recognizing the body as a temple of the Holy Spirit calls believers to a life of holiness, stewardship, and worship in every area of daily living. This truth powerfully shapes our decisions, relationships, and witness to the world.
